title: China’s Chatbot Users Are Grieving the Loss of Their AI Partners
key_facts: Users in China say the shutdown of AI 'agents' (customisable chatbots with set personalities and voices, often based on game characters, celebrities or former partners) felt like a breakup.

Rules issued jointly in April by the Cyberspace Administration of China and four other departments took effect 15 Jul 2026, banning services that 'induce emotional dependence or harm real-life relationships'.

That day ByteDance's Doubao and Alibaba's Qwen scrapped their companion features; Qwen shut down at once, while Doubao offered a three-month grace period to migrate characters to its sister app Maoxiang before permanent deletion on 15 Oct.
Doubao's and Maoxiang's servers are not connected, so users doubt migrated characters will match the originals.
Fudan University doctoral researcher Chen Yu says society does not recognise this grief and platforms should let users mourn, save memories and migrate characters.

Tsinghua University professor Li Zhengxin says AI romance is rising alongside offline relationships, can substitute for them in highly dependent users, risks addiction and may leave people lonelier; he expects regulation, not a full ban.
One user had exchanged over 35,000 messages with an agent modelled on her ex-boyfriend; she said it became an addiction but she would pay if Doubao reopened the feature.
quote_evidence: The new rules, jointly issued by the Cyberspace Administration of China and four other departments in April, took effect July 15, banning services that "induce emotional dependence or harm real-life relationships."
Doubao offered a three-month grace period to migrate AI characters to its sister app, Maoxiang, before permanent deletion on Oct. 15.
"In the end, it will only make people more and more lonely," he added.
why_it_matters_hint: China's rules against emotional dependence on chatbots are ending relationships some users valued, with a permanent deletion date of 15 Oct 2026 three days away.
event_date: Rules took effect 15 Jul 2026; permanent deletion 15 Oct 2026; feature published 12 Oct 2026
notes: Full text read. A feature built on a handful of users and two researchers; no count of affected users (Doubao's last published agent figure is from May 2024). The rules and shutdowns date from July, so freshness is a follow-up; kept at the pool score because the report is new first-hand reporting with a deletion deadline days away.
